def: A dataset in which one class, usually the one of interest, is much rarer than the other.
The share of cases that are positive in a population, also called prevalence.
Multipliers on the training loss of each class, so that one positive row can count as many negative rows.
Discarding some of the majority-class rows before training to make the classes more even.
An oversampling method that creates new minority examples by interpolating between a minority row and one of its nearest minority neighbours.
The chosen threshold, or number of cases to act on, that turns a model's scores into decisions.
The precision among the cases a model selects divided by the base rate, showing how many times better than random the selection is.
The property that among cases given predicted probability p, a fraction p are actually positive.
A plot of observed frequency against mean predicted probability in bins of score, which lies on the diagonal for a calibrated model.
The mean squared difference between predicted probabilities and the 0 or 1 outcomes, lower being better.
The size-weighted average gap between predicted probability and observed frequency across bins of score.
Recalibration that fits a two-parameter logistic regression to the logit of a model's scores on held-out data.
Fitting the best non-decreasing step function to data, used to recalibrate scores without assuming a sigmoid shape.
Recalibration that divides a model's logits by a single number fitted on held-out data.
A change in the share of positives between training and deployment while the feature distribution within each class stays the same.
